body:
FOR N-42 (the item is filed in the lead's PR #112 and is not on main yet, so this note sits on P2-29; it moves to N-42 when #112 is in). DRAWN 17 Nov 2026 (design PR, docs only; nothing built, nothing walked).

FRAMES. S-95 in screens-first-run-and-settings.html: "dlnote" import-elsewhere (case 1), import-failed (2), import-late and "dllock" import-late (3, shade and lock screen), import-stalled (4, the card). S-60 in screens-player-together-and-more.html: "import" stalled (4, the page). S-92: "perm" notif-asked-import (5).

STRINGS (English; Arabic is in the frames).
1. Running card "Downloading Prog snob" / "Downloading to this phone Â· 12 of 24" (S-16's own line for a server that has everything, word for word; bar 75 %) beside the existing "Import stopped" / "Prog snob: 24 songs stay in your library. The rest were not fetched." Stopped on this phone: still no card.
2. "Import could not finish" / the same second sentence. No reason: GET imports carries none.
3. The ordinary end-of-import card: "Prog snob is ready" / "217 of 217 songs are in your library now." No time (GET imports has no finished-at).
4. Page: "No change for 30 minutes. Your server may still be working." Card: "Prog snob: no change for 30 minutes" / "150 of 214 were ready at 9:03. Your server may still be working. Open Encore to see how far it is now." (posted at 9:33, header "8 min" at 9:41).
5. "Show import progress?" / "While your server saves this playlist, Encore can show one notification with how far it has got. No news or alerts are sent unless you switch them on in Settings." Asked once for the whole app, at the first Download or the first Import; only the words depend on the door.

WHAT THE BUILD MUST DO. (1) Post the result card when the import is stopped elsewhere even though its job is merged with a Download. (2) A failed-state branch in download_card_jobs.dart. READ, not run: the Encore server writes only running, done and stopped for an import (imports/service.py), so this card is dead code until a server writes failed. (3) The phone remembers the imports it followed (a small per-account record: id and last state) so an import that stalled, or was running when the app was killed, gets its card at the first look that finds it ended; cleared when posted; older than 24 hours is not announced. (4) The stall word on the page and the card; the 10 second asking still stops (N-43 removes it).

DECISIONS FOR THE LEAD (all PROPOSED): a. The stalled card STAYS (a dated card, no TTL) instead of going away: this changes PB-43 cost 3 and the lead's ruling (1) of 17 Nov; if refused, build only the page sentence. b. Case 3 needs persistent storage (a migration or a settings key). c. Case 2 is drawn for a state no server writes: keep or drop the frame and the branch. d. Left for the build: the CardBar share-retention test.
